claim: instantOf cuts the fraction to milliseconds because 'that is the one form every browser's parser is specified to read'; the admin parsers call Date.parse on the database's microsecond timestamps directly
evidence: True as a statement of the spec (the ES date-time format has exactly three fraction digits), and harmless: WebKit's parser is documented in source as «more lenient than ES5 by accepting more or less than 3 fraction digits» (parseES5TimePortion, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WebKit/WebKit/main/Source/WTF/wtf/DateMath.cpp), so the admin's direct Date.parse of '…24.796123+00:00' is not a Safari hazard. No finding.

claim: A dropped connection on a supabase-js rpc() comes back as `{ error: { code: '' } }` (not a throw), and POST is never retried by the client
evidence: @supabase/postgrest-js 2.117.1 (the installed version, node_modules/.pnpm/@supabase+postgrest-js@2.117.1/.../dist/index.mjs:418-458) catches the fetch rejection and returns `{ success: false, error: { message, details, hint, code: '' }, data: null, status: 0 }` unless throwOnError; RETRYABLE_METHODS is GET/HEAD/OPTIONS only (:81-85), so an rpc POST is not re-sent.
